q: What is the maximum payload (MTU) of a standard Ethernet frame?
exp: Standard Ethernet allows up to 1500 bytes of payload; the full frame with header and FCS is 1518 bytes.

q: Which field of the IPv4 header has been removed in the IPv6 header?
exp: IPv6 drops the header checksum to speed up router processing; TTL became Hop Limit.

q: What is the maximum number of hops a valid route can have in RIP?
exp: RIP treats a metric of 16 as infinity, so the maximum valid hop count is 15.

q: How many segments are normally exchanged to terminate a TCP connection gracefully?
exp: Each direction is closed separately with a FIN and an ACK, giving four segments.

q: Which device regenerates and retransmits a weakened signal at the physical layer?
exp: A repeater works at the physical layer and amplifies/regenerates signals to extend the cable length.

q: Which kind of noise is caused by the random motion of electrons in a conductor and cannot be eliminated?
exp: Thermal noise exists in all conductors above absolute zero. Crosstalk is coupling between wires, impulse noise is a short spike, induced noise comes from motors and appliances.

q: A file of 50 MB (1 MB = 10⁶ bytes) is sent over a 100 Mbps link at full speed, ignoring overheads. How long does it take?
exp: Size = 50 × 10⁶ × 8 = 400 × 10⁶ bits; time = 400 Mb / 100 Mbps = 4 s.

q: A token bucket differs from a leaky bucket in that the token bucket
options: always outputs at a constant rate
drops every packet that arrives in a burst
allows bursts, by saving tokens during idle periods up to the bucket size
exp: Idle time accumulates tokens, so a burst up to the bucket capacity can be sent at full speed; a leaky bucket never exceeds its fixed output rate.

q: How many addresses are there in the CIDR block 10.0.0.0/8?
exp: A /8 leaves 24 host bits: 2²⁴ = 16,777,216 addresses.

q: A CRC with a generator polynomial of degree 16 guarantees detection of all burst errors of length at most:
exp: A CRC with r check bits detects every burst error of length ≤ r, here 16.

q: Which of the following is NOT a field in the UDP header?
exp: The UDP header has source port, destination port, length and checksum; it has no sequence number.

q: HTTP is a stateless protocol. What is the role of cookies?
options: To maintain state across separate HTTP requests
exp: Cookies store small pieces of data at the client so that a server can recognise a user across stateless requests.

q: A message of 6000 bits is sent over a path of 3 links, each 1 Mbps, with negligible propagation delay. It is split into six packets of 1000 bits using store-and-forward packet switching. What is the total time to deliver it?
exp: Each packet takes 1 ms per link. Total = (packets + links − 1) × 1 ms = (6 + 3 − 1) = 8 ms.

q:
Match the OSI layer with its function.
P. Physical  Q. Data link  R. Network  S. Transport
1. Process-to-process delivery  2. Hop-to-hop frame delivery using MAC addresses  3. Host-to-host routing  4. Transmission of raw bits
exp: Physical sends bits, data link delivers frames hop to hop, network routes host to host and transport gives process-to-process delivery.

q: In a 10 Mbps CSMA/CD LAN the one-way propagation delay between the two farthest stations is 25.6 µs. What is the minimum frame size needed to detect collisions?
exp: Frame transmission time must be ≥ 2Tp = 51.2 µs, so size = 51.2 µs × 10⁷ bps = 512 bits (64 bytes).

q: An IPv4 header carries no options. What value does its HLEN field contain?
exp: HLEN counts 4-byte words; the 20-byte base header gives 20/4 = 5.

q: A TCP sender sends a segment starting at sequence number 4000 and carrying 600 bytes of data. What acknowledgement number will the receiver return when it is received correctly?
exp: The ACK number is the next byte expected: 4000 + 600 = 4600.

q: In active-mode FTP, which port does the server use for the data connection?
exp: FTP uses port 21 for control and port 20 for data in active mode.

q: Run-length encoding of the string AAAABBBCCD gives
exp: Runs: AAAA (4A), BBB (3B), CC (2C), D (1D).

q:
Match the generation with its technology.
P. 1G  Q. 2G  R. 3G  S. 4G
1. LTE  2. AMPS (analog)  3. GSM  4. WCDMA/UMTS
exp: 1G used analog AMPS, 2G used GSM, 3G used UMTS/WCDMA and 4G uses LTE.

q: A 7-bit Hamming code (even parity, parity bits at positions 1, 2 and 4) is received as 0110001. Which bit position is in error?
ARP is used to map:
options: a MAC address to an IP address
a domain name to an IP address
a port number to an IP address
an IP address to a MAC address
exp: The Address Resolution Protocol finds the MAC address that corresponds to a known IP address on the local network.

q: Which of the following addresses can be assigned to a host in the subnet 192.168.4.64/27?
exp: The /27 block is 64–95; 64 is the network address and 95 is broadcast, so 94 is the last usable host address.

q: Which protocol is used for exchanging routing information between different autonomous systems on the Internet?
exp: BGP is the path-vector exterior gateway protocol used between autonomous systems.

q: What is the length of the preamble (excluding the start frame delimiter) in a classic Ethernet frame?
exp: The preamble is 7 bytes of alternating 1010... followed by a 1-byte SFD.

q: Which DNS server provides the final, authoritative mapping for the host names of a domain?
exp: The authoritative name server of a domain stores its actual resource records; root and TLD servers only refer queries onward.

q: A link has a bandwidth of 100 Mbps and a round-trip time of 40 ms. What is its bandwidth-delay product?
In NRZ-I encoding, a bit 1 is represented by
options: a transition in the middle of the bit only
a change (transition) of signal level at the beginning of the bit
exp: NRZ-I (inverted) toggles the level for every 1 and keeps it for 0, so long runs of 0s can still lose synchronisation.

q: An IPv4 datagram of total length 4000 bytes (20-byte header) is sent over a link with MTU 1500 bytes. What is the fragment offset field value of the third fragment?
exp: Each fragment carries 1480 data bytes (offset unit 8 bytes). Third fragment starts at 2960 bytes, so offset = 2960/8 = 370.

q: Four sources of 16 kbps each are multiplexed by synchronous TDM with one bit per slot. What is the duration of one frame?
exp: Each source produces one bit every 1/16000 s = 62.5 µs, so a frame (one bit from each source) must last 62.5 µs.

q: Which TCP flag is used to abruptly abort or reset a connection?
exp: The RST flag immediately resets the connection, unlike FIN which closes it gracefully.

q: Which port number is used by the SSH protocol?
exp: SSH uses TCP port 22; 21 is FTP, 23 Telnet and 25 SMTP.

q: In IEEE 802.11 infrastructure mode, one access point together with its associated stations forms a:
exp: An AP and its associated stations constitute a BSS; several BSSs joined by a distribution system form an ESS.

q: A line reduces the power of a signal from 100 mW to 1 mW. What is the attenuation?
exp: dB loss = 10 log10(P1/P2) = 10 log10(100) = 20 dB.

q: A 2D even-parity scheme is used on a 4 × 4 block. The receiver finds that the parity of row 2 and of column 3 is wrong. Which data bit is in error?
exp: The single bad bit lies at the intersection of the failing row (2) and failing column (3).
